title: JAD remote entry
description: <remotes folder>/<name>.json: another JAD server this one may call with profile_message, subagent, profile (info only), transcript and transcripts. The file name (without .json) is the remote's name, written remote:<name>/... in a tool call. It holds no model, tools or instructions, and never the token itself. Two shapes, by the layout of the JAD that reads it. Workspace layout (v2): a BINDING, one server and one workspace on it (remote.workspace, required); it has no credential: the caller's key (G/auth/keys/<key>.json, see remote-key.schema.json, named in remote_keys of workspace.json, a session or a profile) supplies the token, and token_env, token_file and default_session are refused; a session is always written in the address, remote:<name>/<session>/<category>/<profile>. v1 layout: the file holds token_env or token_file (exactly one) and may hold default_session; workspace is refused. A remote is reached over plain http or a unix socket: the bearer token travels in clear text over http, so put that connection behind a VPN or use a unix socket. There is no TLS and no proxy.

url.description: http://host[:port] or unix:///absolute/path.sock. https is refused. No path, query, fragment or credentials. The token of an http url travels in clear text. A unix socket or a loopback address is treated as a server on this machine (its sub-agent calls take the local checkpoint and run to their end); this is a heuristic about the address, not confinement: a name or LAN address of this machine, a tunnel, or a shared file system is not detected.

workspace.description: Workspace layout only (required there, refused in v1): the id of the workspace on that server this binding reaches, as the server's /api/workspaces lists it. A second workspace on the same server is a second binding. The server's token row for the caller's key must name the same workspace.

token_env.description: v1 layout only (removed in the workspace layout: use a key file). Name of the environment variable, which must start with JAD_REMOTE_ (a remote file cannot read provider keys or other variables), that holds the bearer token (at least 32 printable characters). Set exactly one of token_env and token_file.

token_file.description: v1 layout only (removed in the workspace layout: use a key file). File that holds the token, relative to this file or absolute. On unix it must not be readable by group or others.

max_response_bytes.description: Largest response body accepted; a larger one is an error, never a cut. A run view asks for no more text than fits this size (JSON-escaped), and the whole answer of a cut view is read from the remote in parts of this size into the async result file. Default 1048576.

retries.description: Retries of a request that failed to connect or got a 5xx (a send repeats with the same request id, so the remote never starts it twice). Default 2.

max_in_flight.description: Most requests to this remote at the same time. Default 8.

poll_ms.description: Longest one status poll of a remote run waits on the remote. Default 20000.

lost_after_ms.description: How long a remote run may be unreachable before its handle becomes lost. Default 60000.

default_session.description: v1 layout only (removed in the workspace layout: write the session in every address). Session on the remote used when a target is written remote:<name>/<category>/<name>. A session id, or <workspace>:<session> for a remote server that serves several workspaces (the workspace is the id /api/workspaces of that server lists). A target may name a session the same way: remote:<name>/[<workspace>:]<session>/<category>/<name>; <workspace>: is needed when that session id exists in more than one workspace of the remote, otherwise the remote answers ambiguous_session. A remote entry reaches every workspace of the server it points to, as far as the token's globs allow, so an entry that points at this same server is an explicit way across workspaces.

profiles.description: Globs of category/name (no [classes]; '*' does not cross '/') that narrow what a model here may reach on this remote (never widens the remote token's own rights).
